notes: UPDATED 2026-08-06 (second research session): sides/drinks/sauces/add_ons/currency/option_groups below were RESOLVED this session via live POST /api/product calls (see api-map.md 'Product detail endpoint' and unresolved-items.md item #1's resolution) - they were 'inferred_unresolved'/'not_observed' as of the first session, which only had getProductsByCategory evidence.

Every mapping below points at a field observed in a REAL, live getProductsByCategory (or getMenu, or validateLocation, or product) response body from https://saudi.hardees.me during this investigation - see research/api-map/investigation-log.md and research/api-map/api-map.json for the exact endpoint/request each field came from.

Nothing here is copied from competitors/kfc/research/api-map/field-map.json. Hardee's runs on the same 'AMR' (Americana Restaurants) backend platform as KFC (both apps' getAppConfig responses expose 'amr':{...}, and Hardee's own localStorage.profileDraft carries 'appbundle':'com.kfc.me' - a shared mobile bundle id across brand apps), which explains the family resemblance in endpoint NAMES, but the actual field names, nesting, and several sentinel values differ - each mapping below was independently confirmed against a live Hardee's response.

Hardee's products nest THREE possible levels: a top-level 'bundle_group' wrapper product (the one shown in the category grid, e.g. a combo/box/deal card) -> its 'items[]' array of the actual purchasable product(s) inside it -> each item's own 'steps[]' (build customization) and 'variants[]' (size/flavor). A 'simple' typeId product has no items[] wrapper - the top-level object IS the product. Field mappings below note which level they were observed at.
'not_observed' means the field was actively looked for in real responses and was not present/populated - it does not mean the endpoint was never called.

product_id.path: products[].id (top-level, or products[].items[].id for the item nested inside a bundle_group wrapper)
product_id.note: Three different numeric ids can all describe 'the same visual card' - see investigation-log.md 'Nested product identity'. The collector must decide, and document, which one it treats as canonical (recommend: the top-level card id, since that is what the category grid and cluster/aKey are keyed on). RESOLVED 2026-08-06, CORRECTED 2026-08-06 (Streamlit-integration session): for calling POST /api/product on a bundle_group wrapper, do NOT send the wrapper's own `selectedItem` field value directly - `selectedItem` is that item's **sku**, not its **id** (a documentation error caught by a live smoke test - see api-map.md 'Product detail endpoint' correction note). The real rule: find the entry in the wrapper's own `items[]` array whose `sku` equals `selectedItem`, and send THAT entry's `id` (live-confirmed: wrapper 77772960's selectedItem=945 (a sku) -> items[] entry with sku=945 has id=12187 -> /api/product with id=12187 returns real data; id=77772960 or id=945 both return an empty data:{}). Switching a SIZE variant inside the product modal re-issues /api/product with a DIFFERENT nested item id for that size (e.g. Large -> id=12189) - see api-map.md 'Product detail endpoint'. Reference implementation: services/menu_service.py::resolve_detail_lookup_id().

sku.note: Numeric in every sample observed; a few desserts/drinks (e.g. 730008, 610021) use a longer numeric SKU that looks like a POS/SDM item code rather than a small sequential id - do not assume a fixed digit length.

product_name_ar.notes: getMenu/getProductsByCategory were called with Language:'En' throughout this investigation (per the site's own default request payload) and returned no parallel *_ar product name field on any sampled product; category objects likewise had no name_ar. A dedicated Arabic-locale request/response pair was not captured live - see unresolved-items.md.

description_en.example: "A box that's guaranteed to make you laugh ... Terms & conditions apply."

description_ar.notes: Same as product_name_ar - no *_ar description field was present in any live En-locale response captured.

category_id.path: products[].categories[] (on nested items) or the getProductsByCategory response's own top-level data.id

category_name_en.path: getProductsByCategory response's top-level data.name / getMenu's categories[].name

currency.path: products[].currency (only present in the POST /api/product response, NOT in getProductsByCategory's response)
currency.note: UPDATED 2026-08-06 (second research session): getProductsByCategory genuinely never carries this field, as originally found - but POST /api/product (see product_id below) does, on every product checked. A collector calling getProductsByCategory alone still cannot read a currency field and must hardcode SAR; one also calling /api/product per product gets it directly.

regular_price.path: products[].originalPrice (or products[].items[].originalPrice for a nested item)

special_price.note: SENTINEL: 0 is used on 'bundle_group' wrapper products that DO carry a real positive promoId (e.g. id 77772960: originalPrice=39, specialPrice=0, promoId=17237) - live-confirmed on 8+ products across 3 categories. This is the exact same '0 does not mean free, it means this endpoint does not carry a simple fixed-discount price for this bundle shape' pattern documented for KFC, independently re-observed here - see api-map.md quirks section. Simple/single-item products' specialPrice equals originalPrice (e.g. 29/29) when no discount is active.

effective_price.notes: No single field is literally named an 'effective price'. The collector must compute it itself: effective_price = specialPrice if (0 < specialPrice < originalPrice) else originalPrice - mirroring the specialPrice sentinel rule above. Not yet implemented/tested in code, only established from response data during this research phase.

discount_amount.notes: Not a raw field. Would be computed as originalPrice - specialPrice once effective_price's sentinel rule is applied; not verified against a real discounted product's math in this phase beyond simple subtraction.

discount_percentage.path: products[].items[].disPercentage (nested item level - NOT reliably present at the top-level bundle_group wrapper, which showed "" empty string even when specialPrice/promoId indicated an active promo)
discount_percentage.example: "" observed empty on every sampled product in this run - see unresolved-items.md; the field exists and is a string type (matches KFC's '33% OFF' shape) but no live sample with a non-empty value was captured. Do not assume it is unused - only that this run's sample did not surface one.

promo_id.note: SENTINEL: -1 means 'no active offer' - live-confirmed on 7+ products (e.g. id 9074, 9107, 9099, 9097, 9062, 9103, 9096 all promoId=-1 with specialPrice==originalPrice). Any other value is a real, positive promo id shared by every product/item that belongs to the same deal. Identical sentinel convention to KFC, independently re-verified here.

limited_offer.note: 1 observed on every sampled product/item inside category 1480 'Deal of the Day' and several items had an additional 'displayDay' object (see offer.offer_type below) scoping which day(s) of the week the deal is active.

product_type.path: products[].productType (nested item level, numeric) and products[].typeId / .bundleTypeId (string, both top-level and nested)
product_type.note: Hardee's uses a DIFFERENT typeId/bundleTypeId vocabulary than KFC's ('bundle_group' for a combo/box/deal wrapper vs KFC's plain 'bundle') - do not reuse KFC's normalizer logic verbatim.

bundle_type.example: "bundle_group" (combo/box wrapper) | "bundle" (a single sandwich that still has condiment steps)
bundle_type.note: Confusingly, even a plain single sandwich (typeId='simple') carries bundleTypeId='bundle', because it still has a 'Choose your condiments' step - 'bundle' here means 'has customization steps', not 'is a multi-item combo'. Only bundleTypeId='bundle_group' reliably means an actual combo/box/multi-item deal.

availability.path: products[].services (or products[].items[].services): {carhop, del/delevery, din/dine_in, drivethru, tak/take_away}, each 0|1
availability.note: NOTE the misspelling 'delevery' (not 'delivery') on the PRODUCT/category services object specifically - getStoreList's own store-level services object correctly spells 'del' as its short key, and getMenu's category services object also uses 'delevery'. This is a genuine, verified spelling quirk in the live API, not a typo introduced here - see api-map.md quirks section. A collector reading this field must use the exact misspelled key.

calories.notes: products[].nutrition_facts was an empty array on every one of the 100+ products sampled live across all 12 categories, exactly like KFC. UNLIKE KFC, this investigation additionally found and live-verified a separate endpoint, POST /api/getNutritionInfo (empty payload {}), which returns {"location": "<URL of a static Nutritional_Info PDF>"} - i.e. Hardee's publishes nutrition as one whole-menu PDF document, not per-product structured data. See api-map.md and unresolved-items.md.

variants.path: products[].variants[] (top-level) or products[].items[].variants[] is NOT used - variants live on the wrapper, not the nested item, in every sample seen

sizes.note: Standalone drinks (Desserts & Beverages category) do NOT use a size variant at all - each size is instead its OWN separate product/SKU (e.g. id 9000 'Pepsi Medium', a distinct product from a hypothetical 'Pepsi Large'). Size-as-variant only appears on combo/box wrapper products. See unresolved-items.md.

option_groups.path: products[].steps[] (top-level or nested item) - {id, compId, title, subtitle, type: 'radio'|'checkbox'|'stepper', minimum, maximum, isAddon, isModifier, isDependent, isHidden, isTopping, ingredient}. RESOLVED 2026-08-06: getProductsByCategory's steps[] carry ONLY this shell (no options[]) - but POST /api/product's steps[] carry the SAME shell PLUS a fully populated options[] (and each option's own subOptions[] for a Regular/Extra quantity tier) - see api-map.md 'Product detail endpoint' and research/shared/sample-responses/product-endpoint-resolved.json.

included_items.path: products[].items[] (for a bundle_group wrapper) and, within a box product, products[].steps[] entries with isDependent/ingredient describing what a given step contributes
included_items.example: see 'Boxes' category id 664, product 12187 'Roast Beef Box - Regular'

sides.path: POST /api/product's response, products[].steps[] entries titled 'Choice of side item'/'Select your favorite ... side item', .options[] = {title, price, sku, defaultSelected}
sides.example: "Regular Crispy Curls":0, "Reg Spicy Skin Fries":2, "Addon Loaded Fries":7 (SAR)
sides.note: RESOLVED 2026-08-06 via live POST /api/product on a box/meal wrapper's nested item (id=12187 'Roast Beef Box - Regular') - a full 6-option side list with per-option upcharge prices. NOT visible from getProductsByCategory alone - see option_groups above and unresolved-items.md history.

drinks.path: POST /api/product's response, products[].steps[] entries titled 'Choice of Beverages'/'Select your favorite ... beverage', .options[] = {title, price, sku, defaultSelected}
drinks.note: RESOLVED 2026-08-06, same call as sides above - 6 beverage options with per-option upcharge prices. Standalone drink SKUs sold outside a box (Pepsi Medium, etc., category 670) remain separately observed too - see sizes below.

sauces.path: POST /api/product's response, products[].steps[].options[] under a 'Choose your condiments' step, each option = {title, price, defaultSelected, sku, subOptions:[{title:'Regular'|'Extra', price}]}
sauces.example: "Swiss Cheese": defaultSelected, price 2.5 (Extra: also 2.5); "Pickles": not default, price 3 (Extra: 6); "Tomato"/"Onion"/"Ketchup": free (price 0)
sauces.note: RESOLVED 2026-08-06 - see api-map.md 'Product detail endpoint' for the full 15-condiment list observed on a real burger (id 9074), and unresolved-items.md's prior entry for exactly what was missing before (categoryId + service fields on the request).

add_ons.path: POST /api/product's response, products[].steps[] entries titled 'Add Ons', .options[] = {title, price, sku, defaultSelected}
add_ons.example: "No Add On":0, "Spicy Powder":2, "Nacho Cheese Bites (3 pcs)":7, "Churros Caramel Sauce":7 (SAR)
add_ons.note: RESOLVED 2026-08-06, same call as sides/drinks above - an 11-option Add Ons list. `defaultSelected:1` appeared on MOST options simultaneously within this step (not just one) - see api-map.md quirks; do not treat defaultSelected as a reliable single-choice indicator for a radio-type step.

updated_at.path: products[].updatedAt (top-level, category-level; not consistently present per-product) or products[].items[].createdAt

offer_id.path: same as product.promo_id - Hardee's has no separate 'offer' object distinct from a product carrying a promoId; an 'offer' IS a product/category with promoId != -1

offer_name.path: products[].name (top-level wrapper) e.g. 'Foodie Mix', or products[].items[].metaKeyword[] e.g. 'Foodie Mix - Regular'

offer_description.example: "Saturday Deal - Double Cheeseburger + Original Wraptor + Fries"

main_item.notes: For a bundle_group deal, items[0] is usually the primary product, but no field explicitly flags one item as 'main' versus 'side' when items[] has more than one entry - not confirmed against a real multi-item items[] array (every live sample captured had exactly one items[] entry, itself an internally-bundled box/combo, not a flat list of a main item plus separate sides).

included_items.path: products[].items[] and, for a box, its own products[].items[].steps[]

number_of_pieces.notes: No field like 'pieceCount'/'numberOfPieces' was present on any chicken/bucket-style product sampled (Hand Breaded Chicken category, 18 products) - piece count appears only in free-text within name/description (e.g. product names mentioning '2 Tenders'), never as a structured integer.

sides.path: same as product.sides - live-confirmed on a promotional item too ('Double Treat Meal', category 662, wrapper id 77772554 -> nested item 10545), which carried TWO independent side-choice steps ('Select your favorite first/second side item')

drinks.path: same as product.drinks - the same 'Double Treat Meal' promo item carried TWO independent beverage-choice steps

sauces.path: same as product.sauces - the promo item carried FOUR independent condiment steps (one pair per sandwich)

saving_amount.notes: Not a raw field - would be computed as originalPrice - specialPrice; not separately verified.

discount_percentage.note: see product.discount_percentage - empty string in every sample captured live in this run

offer_type.note: Live-confirmed on 'Foodie Mix' (id 77773067, category 1480 'Deal of the Day'): a day-of-week + time-window scoped promotion. This is a genuine Hardee's-specific quirk not seen in KFC's mapping - a collector must NOT assume a promoId active today stays active tomorrow. See api-map.md quirks and unresolved-items.md 'Progressive promotions'.
